title: Lakehouse table formats and query planning in large data lakes
text: [PAGE 1] The synthetic lakehouse benchmark uses 8 worker nodes and 40 simulated workloads. Partition pruning reduced scanned files by 29 percent in the toy experiment; this is invented demo evidence. Study limitations: synthetic queries and unreported variance. [PAGE 2] A table-format comparison explored metadata and optimization tradeoffs. No real-world performance claims may be inferred from this fixture.

title: Adaptive Spark and Iceberg optimization for scalable lakehouse systems
text: [PAGE 1] Synthetic methodology: adaptive compaction selected candidate partitions using a cost heuristic. Results were compared with static compaction in illustrative workloads. Evidence quality is limited because no raw evaluation log accompanies this invented text.

title: Distributed lakehouse query execution using columnar storage
text: [PAGE 1] Synthetic experiment: three table layouts on simulated query workloads. Reported median run time 12, 15, and 19 arbitrary units. These numbers are fictional and useful only for pipeline testing. Limitation: no data provenance and no statistical confidence intervals.
